name: Kulung (Nigeria)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Isa, Adamu Haliru. 2016. A syntactic analysis of Kulung language. PhD thesis, Department of African Languages and Cultures, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. xxiii+298 pp. (ABU Kubanni repository, handle 123456789/9525)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.7 'Kulung Tone Systems' (p.13) gives a three-level tone system (H/M/L, minimal pair nà 'say' / ná 'mother'); sec. 1.8 (pp.13-24) covers consonants, vowels, syllable types (CV, CVV, CVC, CVVC). No mention of word stress/accent anywhere (grep for stress/accent/prominence in a phonological sense: zero). p.8: 'At the moment there is no acclaimed work on the phonology of Kulung.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2026. The Jarawan Bantu languages in Nigeria; what is new research telling us? Jos Linguistic Circle, 15 July 2026 (academia.edu text capture held in sibling dir).
sources.note: Nothing on Kulung prosody. Notes that a Kulung dictionary left in manuscript by Ira McBride 'was edited and published by Uli Kleinwillinghofer and Jorg Adelberger' and that Christopher Green (Syracuse) 'has been working remotely on Mbat, Galamkya, Kulung'. Phonology given only for Labir (three level tones).

sources.citation: Van de Velde, Mark & Dmitry Idiatov. 2022. A first analysis of Mbula (Jarawan, Nigeria). Slides, Banto1d conference, Hamburg.
sources.note: Nothing on Kulung; one Kulung lexical citation ('coal' (ŋ)kala). Describes Mbula, a different Jarawan language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: new data and its relation to Bantu. Working document (20 pp.), Cambridge; comparative wordlists incl. Kulung (UKW data, early 1990s).
sources.note: Nothing; Kulung appears only as a wordlist column; no prosodic statements.

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1988. A note on verbal extensions in Jarawan Bantu. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 3-8.
sources.note: Nothing; Kulung only listed in the classification (group E); 'heavy' refers to Jaar verb-stem weight, not stress.

sources.citation: ANR project JARAWA (PI Mark Van de Velde, LLACAN, from Jan 2026): planned grammar sketches of three Jarawan languages besides Mbula.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: If Kulung is among the sketched languages, it would provide a modern first-hand prosody statement; nothing published yet.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. (Syracuse University): unpublished/ in-progress work on Kulung phonology (Blench 2026 reports Green 'working remotely on Mbat, Galamkya, Kulung' and compiling a comparative Jarawan database); cf. Green 2020 LLA 6 and NLLT on Mbat prosodic structure.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Green's Mbat papers treat syllable and prosodic structure in detail; any Kulung counterpart would be the first modern phonological treatment and would supersede Isa 2016.

sources.citation: McBride, Ira E. (ed. Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Jörg Adelberger). Kulung dictionary (McBride's manuscript dictionary, reported as 'edited and published' in Blench 2026); publisher/year not located in DNB, K10plus, Crossref or the Mainz Adamawa site.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Kleinewillinghöfer's editions normally carry a phonological introduction (tone, syllable, possibly stress); the only lexicographic description of Jarawan Kulung and the most likely place for a first-hand prosody statement.
